style: Original artwork. Contemporary reinterpretation of traditional Korean folk painting (minhwa) — the tiger drawn the old minhwa way (big round comical eyes, toothy mischievous grin, bold ink-outlined stripes, slightly cartoonish proportions) — blended with modern cinematic digital illustration of present-day Seoul. Visible hanji paper texture and soft ink wash. Palette: deep indigo-navy night, saffron-orange tiger, cold cyan smartphone glow, warm sodium streetlight amber. ABSOLUTELY NO text, letters, numbers, signs with writing, captions, watermarks, logos, brand marks or app interface text anywhere in the image; phone screens show only abstract glowing light. Keep the top 22% of the frame as calm, mostly empty dark night sky (space for a title added later) and the bottom 10% as a simple dark area. Natural hands with five fingers. Not in the style of any specific living artist.

images.en: A steep zigzag concrete staircase climbing a hillside residential neighborhood of Seoul at about 2 AM: tightly packed old houses, rooftop green water tanks, tangled power lines, a distant city skyline glowing below. A tired young office worker woman in a long padded coat and office lanyard climbs the stairs, head bowed, face lit cold cyan by the smartphone in her hand. At each of three landings of the staircase (near, middle, far) sits the SAME huge minhwa-style tiger wearing an oversized modern streetwear hoodie, each tiger leaning out and holding out a paw with a grin. The woman's tote bag hangs open with only a few white round Korean rice cakes (tteok) left; each tiger already clutches one white rice cake that glows like a little phone screen. Trail of rice-cake crumbs on the steps. The feeling: she is being robbed one small piece at a time.

Inside a small Seoul studio apartment at 2 AM, view from the foot of the bed: a young woman lies under a duvet, face lit cyan by a smartphone held above her face. From the glowing phone screen, like out of a doorway, a huge minhwa-style tiger leans out toward her — its head and one paw emerge from the screen, the paw held palm-up, waiting to be given a white round Korean rice cake (tteok). On her nightstand a plate of white rice cakes is almost empty, and an analog clock face with no numerals shows the late hour by its hands only. Through the window behind, rows of Seoul apartment towers with only a few lit windows. The tiger's stripes subtly look like vertical scroll motion streaks. Mood: playful but uncanny, a villain who never eats you at once.

Bold graphic poster composition: a giant minhwa-style tiger in a modern hoodie lounges on top of a mountain pass made of a stack of enormous dark smartphones layered like ridges of a Korean landscape painting, against a deep indigo night sky with a large pale moon. Far below at the foot of the phone-mountains, a tiny Seoul street with a lone commuter carrying a basket. A winding path climbs the phone-ridges, and on the path at intervals lie glowing white round rice cakes (tteok) like stepping stones leading up into the tiger's open, grinning mouth. Pine trees and stylized minhwa clouds framing the sides. Strong silhouette, high contrast, readable at small size.
